prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.62
  gal: 0.38
</profile>

Summary of key proposals (ideological framing removed)

- Economy and tax: Invest in green infrastructure, skills and innovation; repair EU trade ties; fiscal rules to reduce debt share and align day-to-day spending with tax revenue. Reverse bank tax cuts; one-off windfall tax on oil and gas; raise Digital Services Tax to 6%; reform capital gains; 4% levy on FTSE-100 buybacks. Target future income tax cut by raising personal allowance. Expand British Business Bank. Universal digital literacy target; clearer consumer T&Cs. Financial inclusion strategy; protect access to cash and banking hubs. Nationwide gigabit broadband.

- Business and jobs: Industrial strategy; replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; prompt-payment enforcement; local banking; scale-up finance. AI cross-sector regulation and UK role in global standards. Trade policy with full Parliamentary oversight and SME support. Worker Protection Enforcement Authority; living wage review. Modernise rights: “dependent contractor” status, fair tax/NI for freelancers, zero-hours protections, flexible parental leave/pay from day one, reformed Statutory Sick Pay.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% renewable electricity by 2030. Ten-year home energy upgrades; zero‑carbon new buildings; social energy tariff; decouple electricity prices from gas. Rooftop solar expansion; maintain fracking ban; no new coal; end fossil-fuel subsidies with just transition. Invest in storage, hydrogen, interconnectors; enable community energy; reform grid and local networks. Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism; industrial decarbonisation support.

- Health and care: Right to a GP within 7 days (24 hours urgent), +8,000 GPs; NHS dentistry access (contract reform, urgent care guarantees); mental health hubs for youth and regular check-ups; 62‑day cancer treatment guarantee; tech upgrades and interoperable records; public health measures. Social care: free personal care; workforce plan; Royal College of Care Workers; Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); unpaid carers’ leave and respite; national standards; portability; kinship care support; ageing and falls prevention.

- Education and skills: A mental health professional in every school; real-terms per‑pupil funding rises and repair backlog cleared; tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils; extra early-years hours and higher Early Years Pupil Premium; restore university maintenance grants; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aim £10,000); teacher workforce plan and funded pay; curriculum and SEND reforms; arts in EBacc; strengthened careers; Erasmus+ return.

- Families and welfare: Free school meals for all children in poverty; parental pay/leave day-one rights incl. self‑employed; double maternity/shared parental pay to £350/week; 90% pay and an extra month for partners; paid neonatal leave. Abolish two‑child limit and benefit cap; 5‑day UC wait; scrap bedroom tax; replace sanctions; disability benefit assessment reform; triple‑lock pensions; WASPI compensation; higher and broader Carer’s Allowance.

- Crime and justice: Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance at burglaries; invest to cut court backlogs; rehab and resettlement. Online Crime Agency; scrap Police & Crime Commissioners; address disproportionality; domestic abuse specialists. Halve time from offence to sentencing; youth diversion; fraud reimbursement and transparency; stronger modern slavery enforcement; prison staffing, training and “through-the-gate” support.

- Environment and farming: New water regulator; ban bonuses until sewage discharges/leaks end; sewage tax; binding 2030 targets for bathing waters; real‑time spill data. Double nature by 2050; 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act; stronger OEP/EA/NE; expand accessible green space; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; deposit return scheme; cut single‑use plastics. National Food Strategy; extra £1bn/year for ELMs; high standards in trade; EU vet/plant agreements; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; animal welfare bill and antibiotic limits.

- Housing and local government: Build 380,000 homes/year including 150,000 social; ten garden cities; empower councils to buy land at existing use value; brownfield incentives; “use‑it‑or‑lose‑it” permissions; zero‑carbon new homes; cladding removal at no cost to leaseholders. End no‑fault evictions; default three‑year tenancies; national landlord register; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; rent‑to‑own; end rough sleeping and scrap the Vagrancy Act. Multi‑year council funding; local powers over second homes/short lets (up to 500% council tax, new planning class); rural fuel duty relief; post offices as hubs.

- Transport: Accelerate EV charging; 5% VAT on public charging; restore 2030 ZEV mandate; plug‑in grant. Freeze rail fares; simplify ticketing; rail electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail, accessibility; light rail; freight shift; £2 bus cap and franchising powers; active travel networks; more local road maintenance. Aviation: higher taxes on frequent flyers/private jets; emissions disclosure; ban short flights where rail <2.5h; moratorium on net airport expansion.

- Culture, media, sport: Protect BBC/S4C/Alba/Channel 4; creative enterprise zones; Creative Europe; EU touring arrangements; tourism minister; accessibility quotas for on‑demand; Leveson Part Two; anti‑SLAPP law; gambling levy, ad restrictions and affordability checks; independent football regulator.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; move work/student visa policy from Home Office; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; safe and legal routes; 3‑month decision service standard; right to work after 3 months. Flexible visa thresholds; exempt NHS/care from Skills Charge and allow dependants; expand Youth Mobility; reverse family income threshold rise. Settled Status protections and physical proof; Windrush redress; firewall on data‑sharing; reduce detention with 28‑day limit; 60‑day move‑on for refugees.

- Rights and political reform: Uphold Human Rights Act/ECHR; race equality strategy; classify misogyny as hate crime; ban conversion practices; right to flexible/remote work for disabled; Digital Bill of Rights; Istanbul Convention delivery. Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; votes at 16; scrap voter ID; cap donations; codify Ministerial Code; Lords reform; stronger transparency and lobbying rules; citizens’ assemblies; federal constitutional reform and enhanced devolution.

- Defence and international: Reverse Army cuts (aim >100k); increase defence spending towards 2.5% GDP; maintain nuclear deterrent; tighter arms export controls; procurement reform; better housing and support for forces and veterans. Rebuild EU ties via agencies, veterinary and mutual recognition deals, then seek Single Market membership long term; support Ukraine including using frozen Russian assets; restore 0.7% ODA and independent department; ceasefire and two‑state process for Israel‑Palestine with recognition of Palestine; targeted human‑rights sanctions; fund BBC World Service.

TEXT_F:
Summary of key policies and commitments (ideological framing removed)

Economy, tax, pensions, childcare
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self-employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT rates stated.
- Triple Lock Plus: uprate State Pension and pensioners’ personal allowance by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%; no new pension taxes; maintain existing pensioner benefits.
- Childcare: 30 hours free for eligible parents from 9 months to school by Sept 2025; nationwide wraparound childcare by Sept 2026.
- Child Benefit based on household income: taper from £120,000 to £160,000.

Work, welfare, carers
- Reform PIP to target genuine needs; expand mental health support; simplify assessments for severe conditions.
- Tighten Work Capability Assessment from Sept 2025; overhaul fit notes to specialist-led.
- Tougher sanctions after 12 months; complete Universal Credit rollout; new Fraud Bill giving DWP HMRC-like powers.
- Continue support for unpaid carers.

Business, SMEs, infrastructure, innovation, trade
- Keep corporation tax; maintain/extend full expensing (to leasing when affordable); SME plan (business rates support, prompt payment enforcement, Open Finance, VAT threshold review, Invest in Women Fund £250m).
- Reallocate £36bn HS2 phase 2 savings to regional transport; nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas; automated vehicles framework; aviation SAF mandate and revenue support.
- Public R&D to £22bn/yr; >£1.5bn for compute; £4.5bn advanced manufacturing.
- Pursue FTAs (India, GCC); implement CPTPP; maintain TCA with EU while protecting sovereignty claims.

Borders, immigration
- Legal annual cap on work and family visas, falling each year and voted by Parliament.
- Health checks pre-travel; higher Immigration Health Surcharge/insurance where needed; raise Skilled Worker thresholds with inflation.
- Rwanda removals with monthly flights; clear asylum claims in 6 months; more returns deals; seek international asylum rule changes; cap for safe/legal routes set by Parliament.

Defence, security, foreign policy, veterans
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; 5% of defence budget for R&D (+2% exploitation); National Defence and Resilience Plan; continued support to Ukraine.
- Veterans Bill; maintain Office for Veterans’ Affairs; visa fee waivers for Commonwealth dependants; benefits disregard for war compensation.

NHS and social care
- NHS funding to rise above inflation annually; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries; 50 more CDCs; 40 hospitals by 2030.
- Dental plan: 2.5m extra appointments; service requirement for new dentists; rural incentives.
- Patient choice across providers; NHS tech £3.4bn (App, AI, data platform); cut 5,500 managers; Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health measures.
- Mental health: school/college teams to 100% by 2030; early support hubs in every community; expand talking therapies by 50%.

Education, skills, youth
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (full-time military/cyber placements or part-time civic service).
- 100,000 additional apprenticeships funded by closing low-outcome degree courses.
- Ban mobile phones during school day; Advanced British Standard for 16–19; 60,000 more SEN places and 15 special free schools.

Policing, justice, protests
- 8,000 extra neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; Martyn’s Law; tougher sentencing (violent/sexual offences, domestic homicides); four new prisons; expand FNO removals; anti-fraud measures.
- New protest powers: restrict face coverings/pyrotechnics; consider cumulative impact; ban protests outside schools.

Energy, net zero, bills
- Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; first CCS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; new nuclear at Wylfa; halve approval times; windfall tax to 2028–29 (subject to prices).
- Bills: maintain price cap; review standing charges; PumpWatch; local electricity markets; £6bn for efficiency plus universal voucher scheme; consent-led onshore wind; solar prioritised on brownfield/roofs; fracking moratorium; import carbon pricing by 2027; UK supply chain bonus in offshore wind.

Housing
- 1.6m homes; lift nutrient neutrality via mitigation fees; fast-track brownfield; densify cities (esp. London); development corporations; protect Green Belt.
- Support buyers: permanent FTB Stamp Duty threshold £425k; new Help to Buy; Mortgage Guarantee continued.
- Leasehold reform (cap ground rents; curb forfeiture; expand commonhold); Renters Reform Bill (abolish Section 21 after court reforms); 2-year CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.

Communities, transport, drivers
- £20m endowments for 135 towns; extend Shared Prosperity Fund three years; more Freeports/Investment Zones.
- Backing Drivers Bill: no road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums on LTNs/20mph; extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament; Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways; nationwide PAYG contactless; parking/pay reforms.

Law, equality, gender
- Clarify Equality Act: sex = biological sex; one legal sex; implement Cass Review; NHS single-sex care rights; parental rights to see curriculum materials.

Rural, farming, fishing, environment, sport, culture
- Farming budget +£1bn over Parliament (inflation-linked); legal food security target and index; fast-track farm infrastructure; five-year tapered seasonal visas; replicate £100m Seafood Fund.
- Plan for Water (tougher penalties, river restoration fund, regulatory reform); maintain record flood defence funding; tree/peat commitments; new National Park; tougher waste crime; prevent new incinerators not yet substantially built.
- Continue grassroots sports facilities funding; independent football regulator; maintain competitive creative tax reliefs; BBC funding review and new complaints process.

Union and devolution
- Extend Shared Prosperity and towns funds UK-wide; protect internal market; specific nation projects on transport, energy and industry; comparable data on public service performance.
